questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨5,-2,3⟩+t⟨0,3,-1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩=-7.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ ⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ 5+3(-2+3t)+(-2)(3-t) & =-7 \\ 5-6+9t-6+2t & =-7 \\ 11t & =0 \\ t & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=0$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5,-2+3(0),3-0⟩ \\  & =⟨5,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5,-2,3).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨2,3,-1⟩+t⟨-1,2,3⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩=11.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩ & =11 \\ ⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩ & =11 \\ -2(2-t)+1(3+2t)+4(-1+3t) & =11 \\ -4+2t+3+2t-4+12t & =11 \\ 16t & =16 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2-1,3+2(1),-1+3(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(1,5,2).$

$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2+3t,2t,2-3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨5,-2,3⟩ & =6 \\ ⟨2+3t,2t,2-3t⟩\cdot ⟨5,-2,3⟩ & =6 \\ 5(2+3t)-2(2t)+3(2-3t) & =6 \\ 10+15t-4t+6-9t & =6 \\ 2t & =-10 \\ t & =-5.\end{aligned}

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-5$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$

\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-2+3(-2),3-2(-2),(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,7,-2⟩\end{aligned}

questions.problem:

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,-1⟩+t⟨5,-2,4⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩=22.
$$
questions.worked_solution:

$$
r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩.

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ ⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ 0(3+5t)+1(-2t)+(-2)(-1+4t) & =22 \\ -2t+2-8t & =22 \\ -10t & =20 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-2),-2(-2),-1+4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,4,-9⟩\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=9-3t \\ y=5+2t \\ z=-7+t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:4x+3y+5z-11=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3y+5z-11 & =0 \\ 4(9-3t)+3(5+2t)+5(-7+t) & =11 \\ 36-12t+15+6t-35+5t & =11 \\ -t & =-5 \\ t & =5\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=5$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=9-3(5)=-6 \\ y=5+2(5)=15 \\ z=-7+5=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(-6,15,-2).$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+y-4z+45 & =0 \\ 3(2-3t)+(-3+t)-4(4+2t) & =-45 \\ 6-9t-3+t-16-8t & =-45 \\ -16t & =-32 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=2$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3(2)=-4 \\ y=-3+2=-1 \\ z=4+2(2)=8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(-4,-1,8).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨4,-2,3⟩+w⟨5,-1,2⟩,\,Π:r=⟨10,-5,12⟩+s⟨4,3,0⟩+t⟨0,2,5⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vector to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨4,3,0⟩\times ⟨0,2,5⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =15i-20j+8k \\  & =⟨15,-20,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =⟨10,-5,12⟩\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨4,-2,3⟩+w⟨5,-1,2⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346 \\ ⟨4+5w,-2-w,3+2w⟩\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346 \\ 15(4+5w)-20(-2-w)+8(3+2w) & =346 \\ 60+75w+40+20w+24+16w & =346 \\ 111w & =222 \\ w & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨4+5(2),-2-(2),3+2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨14,-4,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(14,-4,7).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩,\,Π:r=⟨-5,4,2⟩+s⟨0,3,1⟩+t⟨2,0,1⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨0,3,1⟩\times ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =3i+2j-6k \\  & =⟨3,2,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =⟨-5,4,2⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ ⟨3-2w,1-5w,5+4w⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ 3(3-2w)+2(1-5w)-6(5+4w) & =-19 \\ 9-6w+2-10w-30-24w & =-19 \\ -40w & =0 \\ w & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=0$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨3-2(0),1-5(0),5+4(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,1,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(3,1,5).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+4}{3},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩=39.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(3,1,-4)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨5,2,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨3,1,-4⟩+t⟨5,2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ ⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ (-3)(3+5t)+2(1+2t)-(-4+3t) & =39 \\ -9-15t+2+4t+4-3t & =39 \\ -14t & =42 \\ t & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-3$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-3),1+2(-3),-4+3(-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-12,-5,-13⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(-12,-5,-13).$

$$
l:\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{1}=\frac{z-1}{3},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩=19.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(1,-2,1)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨2,1,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨1,-2,1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ (1+2t)+6(-2+t)+2(1+3t) & =19 \\ 1+2t-12+6t+2+6t & =19 \\ 14t & =28 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),-2+2,1+3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,0,7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(5,0,7).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x-2}{-3}=\frac{y-3}{2}=\frac{z+4}{-1},\,Π:3x-2y+z-38=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(2,3,-4)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨-3,2,-1⟩.$ Therefore, its parametric equations are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨2,3,-4⟩+t⟨-3,2,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2-3t,3+2t,-4-t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-2y+z-38 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+z & =38 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-2,1⟩ & =38 \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-2,1⟩ & =38\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2-3t,3+2t,-4-t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,-2,1⟩ & =38 \\ ⟨2-3t,3+2t,-4-t⟩\cdot ⟨3,-2,1⟩ & =38 \\ 3(2-3t)-2(3+2t)+(-4-t) & =38 \\ 6-9t-6-4t-4-t & =38 \\ -14t & =42 \\ t & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-3$ into the vector equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2-3(-3),3+2(-3),-4-(-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨11,-3,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(11,-3,-1).$

$$

$$

Finally, the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point is obtained by substituting $t=1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5+4(1),3-2(1),-4-3(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨9,1,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(9 , 1, -7).$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations

$$
l: \mathbf{r} = \langle 1,3,1 \rangle + t \langle 2,1,0 \rangle, \qquad  \Pi:4x-3y+2z-7 = 0.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 1+2t , 3+t, 1 \rangle .
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3y+2z-7 & =0 \\ 4x-3y+2z & =7 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 1+2t , 3+t, 1 \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ ⟨1+2t,3+t,1⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ 4(1+2t)-3(3+t)+2\cdot 1 & =7 \\ 4+8t-9-3t+2 & =7 \\ 5t & =10 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),3+(2),1⟩ \\  & =⟨5,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5 , 5, 1).$
